questions.q: Which of these is a physical quantity?
questions.e: Length can be measured and expressed with a unit.

questions.q: Which is NOT a physical quantity?
questions.e: Happiness has no standard physical measurement unit.

questions.q: What is a physical quantity?
o: A measurable property expressed with a number and unit
questions.e: Physical quantities have measurable magnitudes and units.

questions.q: Which quantity is an SI base quantity?
questions.e: Electric current is one of seven SI base quantities.

questions.q: Which is an SI derived quantity?
questions.e: Density is mass divided by volume.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of mass?
questions.e: The SI base unit of mass is kilogram (kg).

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of time?
questions.e: The SI base unit of time is second (s).

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of temperature?
questions.e: The kelvin (K) is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of amount of substance?
questions.e: The mole (mol) is the SI base unit for amount of substance.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of luminous intensity?
questions.e: The candela (cd) is the SI base unit of luminous intensity.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.e: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit of electric current.

questions.q: How many SI base quantities are there?
questions.e: The SI has seven base quantities.

questions.q: Which pair contains only base quantities?
questions.e: Length and time are SI base quantities.

questions.q: Which pair contains only derived quantities?
questions.e: Speed and acceleration are calculated from base quantities.

questions.q: Which is the SI derived unit of force?
questions.e: The newton (N) is the SI derived unit of force.

questions.q: Which is the SI derived unit of pressure?
questions.e: The pascal (Pa) equals one newton per square metre.

questions.q: Which is the SI derived unit of energy?
questions.e: The joule (J) is the SI derived unit of energy.

questions.q: Which is the SI derived unit of power?
questions.e: The watt (W) equals one joule per second.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of area?
questions.e: Area is length multiplied by length, so its unit is m².

questions.q: What is the SI unit of volume?
questions.e: Volume has three dimensions of length, so its unit is m³.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of speed?
questions.e: Speed is distance divided by time.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.e: Acceleration is change in velocity per second.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of density?
questions.e: Density equals mass divided by volume.

Which is a vector quantity?
What distinguishes a vector from a scalar?
o: A vector always has a large value
A vector has magnitude and direction
questions.e: Vectors require both magnitude and direction.

questions.q: Which pair consists of vectors?
questions.e: Force and displacement have directions as well as magnitudes.

questions.q: Which pair consists of scalars?
questions.e: Mass and speed have magnitude only.

Which instrument is most suitable for measuring a pencil length?
questions.e: A metre rule measures ordinary lengths.

questions.q: Which instrument measures short time intervals?
Which instrument is suitable for measuring wire diameter?
questions.e: A micrometer screw gauge measures very small diameters.

questions.q: Which instrument can measure internal diameter of a tube?
questions.e: The inside jaws of vernier calipers measure internal diameter.

questions.q: Which instrument measures the volume of a liquid?
questions.e: A measuring cylinder measures liquid volume.

questions.q: What is least count?
o: The smallest increment an instrument can resolve
The largest value on its scale
questions.e: Least count is the smallest scale increment or resolution.

questions.q: Which reading is more precise if instruments are correctly used?
questions.e: The reading with finer resolution gives more detail, though it need not be more accurate.

questions.q: What does accuracy describe?
o: Closeness to the true or accepted value
questions.e: Accuracy is closeness to the true or reference value.

questions.q: What does precision describe?
o: Closeness to the true value only
Closeness of repeated measurements to one another

questions.q: What is a systematic error?
o: A consistent bias that shifts readings in one direction
A change due only to chance
questions.e: Systematic error produces a consistent offset or bias.

questions.q: What is a random error?
o: Using the wrong unit every time
questions.e: Random errors cause readings to scatter unpredictably.

questions.q: How can random error often be reduced?
o: Repeat measurements and calculate a mean
questions.e: Averaging repeated independent measurements can reduce random effects.

questions.q: What is parallax error?
o: Error from writing too many digits
Error from an incorrect unit conversion
Error caused by viewing a scale from an angle
questions.e: Parallax arises when the eye is not aligned with the reading mark.

questions.q: How should the eye be positioned when reading a scale?
o: Directly in line with the mark
questions.e: Looking straight at the mark reduces parallax error.

questions.q: What is zero error?
o: An error only in digital devices
The last digit of every reading
A nonzero reading when the true input is zero
questions.e: Zero error occurs when an instrument does not read zero for zero input.

questions.q: A positive zero error is corrected by:
o: Subtracting the zero error from the observed reading
questions.e: Corrected reading = observed reading − zero error.

questions.q: What is the usual form of scientific notation?
questions.e: Scientific notation uses a coefficient with magnitude from 1 up to but not including 10.

questions.q: Which is written in correct scientific notation?
questions.e: The coefficient must be at least 1 and less than 10.

questions.q: What does a negative power of ten usually indicate?
o: A larger unit in every case
questions.e: 10 raised to a negative integer is a fraction.

questions.q: What is a significant figure?
o: A digit in the unit symbol
Only a digit after a decimal point
A digit that conveys meaningful measurement precision
questions.e: Significant figures express the precision recorded in a measurement.

questions.q: How many significant figures are in 3.40?
questions.e: The trailing zero after the decimal is significant.

questions.q: How many significant figures are in 0.0045?
How many significant figures are in 5.006?
questions.e: Zeros between nonzero digits are significant.

questions.q: What is the dimension of area?
What is the dimension of volume?
What is the dimension of speed?
questions.e: Speed is distance divided by time.

questions.q: What is the dimension of acceleration?
questions.e: Acceleration is velocity change divided by time.

questions.q: What is the dimension of density?
questions.e: Density is mass divided by volume.

questions.q: What is the dimension of force?
What is the dimension of pressure?
questions.e: Pressure equals force divided by area.

questions.q: What is the dimension of work?
What is the dimension of power?
questions.e: Power is work divided by time.

questions.q: What is the relation between a litre and a cubic metre?
questions.e: One litre is one cubic decimetre, or 10⁻³ m³.

questions.q: Which statement about mass and weight is correct?
o: Mass depends on gravity in the same way as weight
Mass is a scalar and weight is a force
questions.e: Mass is a base scalar quantity; weight is gravitational force.

questions.q: What is the unit symbol for kelvin?
questions.e: Kelvin uses capital K without a degree sign.

questions.q: What is the unit symbol for kilogram?
questions.e: The correct SI symbol is kg.

questions.q: What is the unit symbol for newton?
questions.e: The symbol for the newton is N.

questions.e: The SI unit symbol for second is s.

questions.q: What is the SI symbol for metre?
questions.e: The SI symbol for metre is lowercase m.

questions.q: What is the best way to report a measured length?
o: With a numerical value and unit
questions.e: A measurement needs both magnitude and unit.

questions.q: What is the appropriate instrument for measuring a classroom width?
questions.e: A measuring tape is suitable for lengths of several metres.

questions.q: What is the correct method to read a measuring cylinder?
o: Read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level for water
Read the highest marking regardless of liquid
questions.e: For water, read the bottom of the meniscus at eye level.

questions.q: Why should a measuring cylinder stand vertically?
o: To obtain a reliable liquid-level reading
questions.e: A level upright cylinder helps avoid reading errors.

questions.q: Which instrument can measure both external and internal diameters?
questions.e: Vernier calipers have jaws for both external and internal measurements.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of length?
questions.e: The metre is the SI base unit of length.

questions.q: Which of these is a base quantity rather than a derived quantity?
questions.e: Luminous intensity is an SI base quantity.

questions.q: Which is the unit of frequency?
questions.e: The hertz (Hz) equals one cycle per second.

questions.q: Which is the unit of electric charge?
questions.e: Charge is current multiplied by time; its unit is coulomb (C).

questions.q: Which is the unit of potential difference?
questions.e: Potential difference is measured in volts (V).

questions.q: Which of these is a vector?
Which of these is a scalar?
questions.e: Temperature has magnitude but no spatial direction.

questions.q: Which physical quantity is expressed in kg/m³?
questions.e: Density is mass per unit volume.

questions.q: Which physical quantity is expressed in N/m²?
questions.e: Pressure is force per unit area.

questions.q: Which physical quantity is expressed in J/s?
questions.e: Power is energy transferred per unit time.

questions.q: Which physical quantity is expressed in m²?
questions.e: Area has units of square metres.

questions.q: Which physical quantity is expressed in m³?
questions.e: Volume has units of cubic metres.

Which action can reduce a known calibration bias?

questions.q: Why are standard units important?
questions.e: Agreed units allow measurements to be communicated and compared.

questions.q: What is the purpose of SI prefixes?

questions.e: SI prefixes provide powers-of-ten multiples and submultiples.
